title: Shift handoff, runbook retirement, and status automation bundle
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document codifies a compact, repeatable on-call handoff sequence, a lightweight runbook retirement lifecycle, and an opinionated set of templates and automation snippets for keeping the status page and customer communications accurate during incidents. It is intended for first responders, on-call leads, incident commanders, and the SRE engineers who maintain runbooks.

Scope: Applies to Redwood-hosted services, Dedicated control plane components, and customer-facing public APIs. Private deployments should mirror the same approach unless constrained by customer confidentiality agreements.

Quick reference (single-page)

- Primary SLOs: 99.95% p99 availability monthly for API gateway; latency SLO: 95% < 200ms for metadata endpoints.
- Alert thresholds: Error rate > 0.5% for 5m (P1 candidate); p95 latency increase > 3x baseline for 5m (P2 candidate).
- Escalation: Pager -> Team on-call -> On-call lead -> Incident commander.

Incident severity definitions

1) P0 - System outage: >30% customer impact or global API failure. Requires immediate full-bridge and exec notification.
2) P1 - Major degradation: Significant subset of customers affected, degraded core functionality, remediate within 2 hours.
3) P2 - Partial impact: Regional or non-critical feature regression, target TTR within 24 hours.
4) P3 - Cosmetic or low-priority: Minor bugs, documentation, or background jobs.

Handoff checklist (30–60s read for incoming on-call)

1. Confirm status page: verify there is a current incident or none. Command: curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_API_KEY\" https://status.redwoood.example/api/v1/incidents | jq .active
2. Read the top pager alert: check alert source, service name, and immediate mitigation notes on the alert (pager message).
3. Verify recent playbook steps: open the active runbook URL indicated in the pager (if none, create an incident and attach a new runbook).
4. Confirm slack/bridge and add yourself: #incident-<service> and /join bridge.
5. Update the shift log: add your name, local timezone, and planned check-in cadence.
6. If any escalation has been triggered (escalation level >= 2), meet the on-call lead within 10 minutes.

Minimal triage flow (first 15 minutes)

1) Triage intent: Is this customer-visible?
  - Yes -> proceed to containment (identify proxy, throttle, or rollback).
  - No -> create follow-up ticket and classify as P2/P3.

2) Data collection checklist (commands you will run):
  - kubectl -n <svc> get pods -o wide --selector=app=<svc>
  - curl -v https://<svc>/.health || echo \"health-check-failed\"
  - ./infra/observability/query_histogram.sh --service <svc> --metric requests_latency_p95 --window 10m
  - aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace Redwood/Infer --metric-name ErrorCount --start-time $(date -u -d '10 minutes ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) --end-time $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) --period 60 --statistics Sum

3) Containment patterns (common fast mitigations):
  - Route around unhealthy AZs using traffic-split: edit TrafficSplit weight for region-b;
  - Temporary scale up replica count for autoscaled pools;
  - Use immediate config toggle (feature-flag rollback) to disable failing integration;
  - Revert recent deployment if the release is implicated.

Incident communication bundle

- Status page: Use the provided API snippet to open/update incidents. Keep updates every 15–30 minutes for P0/P1 until mitigation is in place.

API sample (curl)

curl -X POST https://status.redwoood.example/api/v1/incidents \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_API_KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"service":"api-gateway","severity":"major","title":"API error surge affecting requests","impact":"Customers may see increased 5xx errors","status":"investigating","visibility":"public"}'

Patch/update example

curl -X PATCH https://status.redwoood.example/api/v1/incidents/<incident-id> \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_API_KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"status":"monitoring","update":"Mitigation in place: traffic shifted to region-b. Error rate falling."}'

Customer-facing message templates

- Initial public message (short):
\"We are investigating an increase in error rates affecting requests to the Redwood API. Some customers may experience failed requests or timeouts. We will provide updates every 15 minutes.\"

- Messaging when mitigation is in place:
\"Mitigation is in place: traffic has been shifted and error rates are declining. We continue to monitor closely and will provide a post-incident summary.\"

- Private customer outreach (for affected high-tier customers):
\"Hi <Customer Name> — we detected a surge of 5xx responses impacting your requests. We’ve shifted traffic and applied a mitigation; the issue is being monitored. Your CS lead (<cs-lead@redwood.com>) will follow up with a detailed timeline and technical RCA.\"

Runbook retirement lifecycle (why this exists)

Runbooks degrade over time: steps become stale, owners change, and commands rot. This section defines how a runbook is retired, archived, or refreshed so the on-call corpus remains trustworthy.

Criteria to consider a runbook for retirement or refresh:
- No runs in the last 12 months and the service is inactive or deprecated.
- > 3 broken/obsolete commands detected during annual review.
- Ownership undefined for > 60 days after team restructuring.

Runbook retirement process (4-step)

1) Identify candidate: automated scan or manual nomination (tag runbook with "candidate-for-retire").
2) Owner review: current runbook owner must respond within 14 days with either a refresh or agree to retirement.
3) Archive window: if no response, move runbook to Archived space with a notice and TTL 90 days where it is recoverable.
4) Final purge or convert to KB article: after TTL, archived runbooks are deleted from the active corpus and a short KB note is created summarizing the reason and replacement if any.

Runbook review cadence and responsibilities (table)

| Role | Cadence | Responsibility |
| On-call lead | Quarterly | Validate 3 selected high-importance runbooks end-to-end |
| Service owner | Annual | Complete full runbook verification and update |
| Documentation team | Annual | Run cross-service linting and command validation |

Post-incident micro-postmortem template (deliver within 72 hours for P0/P1)

1) Title: <Service> — <Date> — P1/P0
2) Summary (2–3 sentences): one-paragraph customer-facing summary.
3) Timeline: bullets (UTC timestamps) for discovery, mitigation, root cause, and resolution.
4) Impact: quantifiable metrics (requests affected, regional impact, error volume).
5) Root cause & contributing factors: concise bullets.
6) Actions: short-term (today), medium-term (30d), long-term (90d) with owners and target dates.
7) Postmortem review: date/time for cross-team alignment and verify actions closed.

Game day micro-syllabus (2-hour practical run)

Objective: validate handoff, status update cadence, and runbook accuracy.

Agenda:
- 0:00–0:15: Quick brief and roles assigned (IC, comms, responder, observer).
- 0:15–0:45: Inject failure A (latency spike) — run triage, identify mitigation.
- 0:45–1:05: Update status page and issue customer message; observers score clarity.
- 1:05–1:35: Inject failure B (partial outage due to deployment) — perform rollback.
- 1:35–1:55: Run a postmortem mini-write (15m) and present findings.
- 1:55–2:00: Retrospective: 3 takeaways and 2 action items.

Scoring rubric (observer use):
- Hand-off clarity: 0–5
- Runbook fidelity: 0–5
- Status messaging quality: 0–5
- Time to accurate status update: target < 15m

Operational tooling and small automations

- Incident starter CLI: tools/incident create --service api-gateway --severity major --notify-slack #inc-api (wraps the status API above and creates slack bridge).
- Shift log template: tools/shift-log add --name "<Name>" --tz "PST" --notes "coverage through 09:00 UTC"
- Runbook linter (CI): docs-lint --check-runbooks --fix-commands (runs on pull requests that change runbooks).

- This bundle should be reviewed by the on-call leads every 6 months and after any P0 incident.
- Runbook retirement automation will run monthly to surface candidates; owners will be emailed a digest.

Appendix: Common status page templates (raw)

[PUBLIC] Initial update:
{\n  \"title\": \"Investigating increased error rates for <service>\",\n  \"body\": \"We are currently investigating an increase in error rates affecting <service>. Some requests may fail. Our engineers are actively investigating. Updates every 15 minutes.\",\n  \"visibility\": \"public\"\n}

[PUBLIC] Mitigation in place:
{\n  \"title\": \"Mitigation applied for <service>\",\n  \"body\": \"Traffic has been shifted and error rates are declining. We continue to monitor and will share a detailed post-incident summary.\",\n  \"visibility\": \"public\"\n}
